small_guidance:
- The output spatial size is 30×62×62 (M = 16·30·62·62 = 1,845,120) and NN=OC=64 is tiny — most current configs with BLOCK_N=128/256 are wasted. Prune the autotune list to BLOCK_N=64 only, and sweep BLOCK_M ∈ {64,128,256} with BLOCK_K ∈ {32,64,96} (K = 32·27 = 864 — try BLOCK_K=96 since 864 is divisible by it, eliminating tail masking).
- Add configs with num_stages=3/4 for the larger BLOCK_M variants (BLOCK_M=128/256, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32) — the K loop is short (~27 iterations at BLOCK_K=32) so deeper pipelining helps hide x_offset gather latency.
- Hoist the stride constants (ID*IH*IW, IH*IW, IC*ID*IH*IW) into Python-side `tl.constexpr` ints so the index math compiles to immediates, and precompute `kd/kh/kw/ic` as `tl.constexpr` lookup once outside the K-loop is not possible, but you can replace the `//` and `%` by KDHW/KHW with constexpr small-int divisors (already constexpr — verify Triton lowers them to shifts/muls).
large_guidance:
- Switch the GEMM mapping: make N (=OC=64) the K-loop free dim along warp-N and put the spatial+batch axis along M with persistent blocks. Because OC=64 fits in a single BLOCK_N=64 tile, replace the 2-D grid with a 1-D grid over M only (one block per spatial tile computes all 64 output channels), eliminating the num_pid_n dimension and the swizzle overhead.
- Reorganize the K reduction so the inner loop walks (kd, kh, kw) explicitly (27 iters) with IC as the BLOCK_K dimension (IC=32 fits exactly in one BLOCK_K=32 tile). This makes every inner iteration a full unmasked tl.dot of shape [BLOCK_M, 32] × [32, 64] with no K-tail and no divmod in the inner loop — only 3 nested adds for input coordinates.
- Use channels-last input layout (N, D, H, W, C) so the IC dimension is the contiguous one, giving fully coalesced loads along the GEMM-K axis; reshape weight to (KD, KH, KW, IC, OC) once at init. Fuse mish→tanh in the epilogue as today.
